findings.title: Call to non-existent isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() does not compile
findings.body: UsernameForm.authenticate now calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the only method of that name is UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) (declared at UsernamePasswordForm.java:160). Neither UsernamePasswordForm, AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator nor the Authenticator interface defines a no-arg overload, so this class will not compile. Either pass the user (isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())) or add the intended no-arg overload.

findings.title: Conditional passkey UI is no longer enabled for unauthenticated (user == null) logins
findings.body: The new helper returns false whenever user is null because of the trailing `&& user != null`. Both new call sites in this file, authenticate() at line 115 and challenge(context, error, field) at line 137, pass context.getUser(). Before this change fillContextForm() was deliberately called when the user was NOT yet identified (the original code was inside the `user == null` branch and guarded with `context.getUser() == null`). As a result the initial/anonymous login page will no longer render the conditional passkey UI (the `#webauth` form and `autocomplete="username webauth"`), so discoverable-key/passkey autofill login stops working and the feature regresses. This directly contradicts unchanged assertions such as PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey (lines 145-146) and PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey (lines 192-194), which expect the `#webauth` form on the anonymous page. The guard should not depend on user being non-null (fill for both null and non-null users), otherwise re-authentication cannot be fixed without breaking first-time passkey login.

findings.title: reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey does not exercise a user without a passkey
findings.body: The test name promises to cover re-authentication of a user who has no passkey, but the body only disables passkeys for the whole realm via setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE). Since UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user) checks only the realm passwordless policy plus `user != null` and never consults the user's credentials, the actually interesting case - passkeys enabled for the realm, user has no registered passkey, re-authentication page is rendered - is never tested. In that case the passkey control would be offered even though it cannot succeed. Add a test that leaves passkeys enabled and uses an account with no WebAuthn/Passkey credential.
